summary: Huston Smith was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Central Methodist University, University of Chicago, and under Zuigan Goto. He held posts at Denver, Washington University, MIT (1958–1973), Syracuse (1973–1983), and UC Berkeley.

Huynh Kim Lan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where they studied under thesis advisers Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong.
Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, studying under Kapila Abhayawansa.

Hyakudai Sakamoto was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held academic posts at Tokyo University of Pharmacy and Life Sciences (~1956–1969), Aoyama Gakuin University (~1969–1997), and the Open University of Japan (~1997–2000).

Hyejeong Choi, a history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies scholar, earned a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. Later, Choi served as a visiting researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara.

Hyon Gak Sunim is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Yale University, the University of Freiburg, and Harvard University. He also studied under traditional teacher Seungsahn Haengwon from around 1990 to 2004.

Hyoung Seok Ham works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Virginia in 2010 and completed his PhD at the University of Michigan under doctoral supervisor Madhav M. Deshpande.

Hywel David Lewis was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Ysgol Syr Hugh Owen, Bangor University, and Jesus College, Oxford. He served on the faculty at Bangor University from circa 1936 to 1955.

Hürelbaatar Ujeed, a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, earned a Ph.D. in Social Anthropology from the University of Cambridge. He served as Professor and Principle Investigator at Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.
Hōgetsu was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Tongyuan and Zuihe, and later taught Hokai.
Hōin Yamada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University from circa 1959 to 1963 and was a student of Gyōin Hashimoto.
Hōju is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University and KU Leuven, and later taught Kyokuga Saeki.

Ian Harris was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Cambridge and Lancaster University. He taught at St Martin's College (~1986–2007) and became Professor Emeritus at the University of Cumbria.

Ian James Coghlan is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed a doctorate in Asian Studies at La Trobe University in 2004 and served as a research fellow at Monash University's Monash Asia Institute in 2005.
Ian Kishizawa was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saitama University and trained under traditional teacher Sotan Oka. He taught students Shunryu Suzuki and Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani.

Ian Reader is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology who completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Leeds. He held positions at Stirling (~1989–1995) and Lancaster University (~2003–2008), among other institutions.

Ibrahim Shah is an archaeology scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Peshawar under Farid Khan and Ihsan Ali. He became Associate Professor and Department Chairman in Cultural Heritage and Tourism Management at Hazara University.
Ichijo Ogawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Otani University. He held academic posts there from circa 1968 to 2005, serving as university president.

Ichiro Hori was a religious studies, Buddhist studies, and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Kunio Yanagita. He taught at Tohoku University (~1952–1965) and the University of Tokyo (1965–1971).
Ichiro Katayama is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Komazawa and Otani universities under Kogen Mizuno. He was an assistant professor at Komazawa University from 1975 to 2013.
